subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sahrawi Tea: Ceremony in the Desert
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sahrawi Tea: Ceremony in the Desert.

hook.text: In the Western Sahara, nomadic Sahrawi people prepare tea in a ritual that can take over an hour on sand and coals.

buildup.text: Green tea is boiled with a mountain of sugar in a small metal pot, then poured back and forth to create foam.

discovery.text: Three rounds are served with decreasing sugar: the first is sweet, the second moderate, the third barely sweetened.

twist.text: The ceremony happens in desert heat—yet hot tea cools the body by triggering sweat more than cold drinks do.

climax.text: For Sahrawi nomads, the tea ceremony is the social glue that holds communities together across vast, empty landscapes.

punchline.text: Sand, coals, sugar, and hospitality. In the desert, tea is home.

quiz.question: Why does hot tea actually cool the body in desert heat?
options: It triggers sweating that cools the body more effectively than cold drinks
